primitives.name: Spectral Lineup Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: First, our analysis decomposes the team success signal into components that are naturally understood as the contributions of player groups of a given size: individuals, pairs, triples, fours, and full five-player lineups.

primitives.assumptions: Team success is measurable via play-by-play data; contributions are additive and orthogonal across group sizes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When lineup frequency is insufficient for stable estimation of group effects.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper is that team success in basketball cannot be fully captured by individual metrics due to the interdependence of player actions. Spectral analysis offers a method to decompose the team success signal into orthogonal components representing contributions from groups of players. This allows for a clean separation of synergies at different levels (individuals, pairs, etc.), avoiding overlap in attribution. The mathematical structure relies on the assumption that the success signal can be represented as a linear combination of basis functions corresponding to player groupings. Each group's contribution is isolated through orthogonal projection, ensuring that higher-order synergies do not obscure lower-order ones. The failure mode occurs when data is sparse or noisy, leading to ill-conditioned estimates of group contributions. The approach also assumes that lineup effects are stationary over time, which may not hold in practice. The methodology bridges discrete combinatorial structures (player combinations) with continuous signal processing techniques, enabling both descriptive and predictive analytics.
